name: Web and application server
definition: Program that serves websites or runs web applications for clients over a network.

name: Application and infrastructure monitoring software

name: Compatibility layer

name: PC-migration software

name: CAE and simulation software

name: Diagramming software

name: Speech-recognition and dictation software
definition: Program that turns the user's speech into typed text and voice commands.

name: Screenwriting software

name: Show-control software

notes: Giclee print filter on Singulart; glossary: giclee is the French term for inkjet.

name: gelatin silver print
definition: silver halide in a gelatin layer on paper, exposed and developed in a darkroom.
notes: Gelatin silver print named as dominant 20th century process.

name: daguerreotype
definition: an image on a silvered copper plate.
notes: Daguerreotype: sharp images on silver-plated copper, announced 1839.

name: chromogenic print
definition: colour dyes formed in the layers of colour paper by development.
notes: Chromogenic prints use cyan, magenta and yellow layers.

name: dye-transfer print
definition: colour made by transferring dyes from matrices onto paper.
notes: Dye-transfer prints named in guide; no dye-transfer listing fetched.

name: silver dye bleach print
definition: colour dyes already in the paper, bleached away where not wanted.
notes: Ilfochrome photograph for sale; page does not use term silver dye bleach.

name: archival pigment print
definition: a pigment inkjet print of a photograph on fine-art paper.
notes: Archival pigment prints are inkjet with long-life ink.

name: platinum or palladium print
definition: an image in platinum or palladium metal on paper.
notes: Platinum print on gold leaf sold; palladium not shown on page.

name: cyanotype
definition: an iron-salt print giving a blue image.
notes: Handmade cyanotype triptych for sale on 1stDibs.

name: tintype
definition: a positive image on a thin iron plate.
notes: Antique tintype category on 1stDibs with tintype photographs for sale.

name: photogram
definition: an image made without a camera by placing objects on light-sensitive material.
notes: Photogram works listed for sale on 1stDibs.

name: instant print
definition: a self-developing print from an instant camera or film pack.
notes: 278 Polaroid photographs for sale on 1stDibs.

name: bronze sculpture
definition: cast copper-tin alloy, usually patinated.
notes: Bronze is a Singulart sculpture medium; bronze masks and torsos on Artsper.

name: steel and iron sculpture
definition: steel, iron or other ferrous metal welded, forged, cut or bent to form.
notes: Steel, stainless steel and cast iron are Singulart sculpture media.

name: pewter and other cast-metal figurine
definition: an ornamental figure cast in pewter, zinc, tin or another non-bronze metal.
notes: Royal Selangor pewter collectible figurines sold by W Hamond; tin 92-97 percent.

name: stone carving
definition: marble, limestone, alabaster or other stone carved to form.
notes: Stone and marble are Singulart sculpture media.

name: jade carving
definition: a figure or object carved from jade.
notes: Carved jade figures for sale on 1stDibs.

name: wood carving
definition: a figure or sculpture carved from wood.
notes: Hand-carved wood figurative sculptures for sale; Wood is a Singulart medium.

name: ivory and bone carving
definition: a figure or sculpture carved from ivory, bone, horn or antler.
notes: Meiji ivory okimono carvings for sale; Bone is a Singulart medium.

name: terracotta sculpture
definition: modelled or moulded clay fired without a glaze.
notes: Terracotta is a Singulart sculpture medium.

name: glazed earthenware and stoneware sculpture and figurine
definition: a figure or sculpture in glazed fired clay other than porcelain.
notes: 585 glazed ceramic, stoneware and terracotta figurative sculptures for sale.

name: porcelain and bone china figurine and sculpture
definition: a figure or sculpture in porcelain or bone china.
notes: Lladro and Royal Doulton porcelain figurines for sale on 1stDibs.

name: glass and crystal sculpture and figurine
definition: a blown, cast, fused or cut glass or lead-crystal figure or sculpture.
notes: Glass figurative sculptures and Swarovski crystal figurines for sale.

name: resin sculpture and figurine
definition: a cast resin figure or sculpture, usually painted.
notes: Resin is a Singulart sculpture medium; resin figurine shop page not fetched.

name: plaster sculpture
definition: cast or modelled plaster.
notes: Plaster is a Singulart sculpture medium.

name: wax sculpture
definition: modelled or cast wax.
notes: Wax Sculpture for Sale category on Artsper.

name: soft sculpture
definition: a three-dimensional sculpture of fabric, fibre or other soft material, stuffed, wrapped or stitched.
notes: Artsy Soft Sculpture; Textile is a Singulart sculpture medium.

name: found-object assemblage
definition: a sculpture assembled from found, salvaged or discarded objects, or from several materials none of which governs.
notes: Assemblage Sculpture for Sale: Arman, Spoerri, Pras; Reclaimed objects medium.

name: neon sculpture
definition: a sculpture in which a lit gas-discharge tube or an equivalent light source is the medium.
notes: Neon Tube Light is a Singulart sculpture medium.

name: tapestry
definition: a picture or pattern woven on a loom to hang on a wall.
notes: 4,607 woven tapestries for sale on 1stDibs.

name: embroidered picture
definition: a picture worked in thread with a needle on a fabric ground.
notes: Framed needlepoint and embroidery pictures for sale; Artsy Embroidery.

name: brush and pen calligraphy
definition: writing made as the picture, in brush or pen script.
notes: Calligraphy art listings: Chinese ink, Japanese, Arabic; Artsy East Asian Calligraphy.

name: seal carving [篆刻]
definition: script characters carved into a seal of stone or another material as a work of art, sold as the seal or its impressions (provisional until a fetched seller sells it apart from calligraphy).
notes: Hand-carved Shoushan stone seal sold as collectible; sold as the seal.

name: collage
definition: a picture built from pasted or bonded elements (paper, cloth, photographs, found flat material).
notes: Collage is a Singulart painting technique and an Artsy medium.

name: mosaic picture
definition: a picture set in small pieces (tesserae) of stone, glass or ceramic.
notes: Sicis handmade glass mosaic wall piece for sale; Artsy Mosaics.

name: sculpture plinth or stand
definition: a base, plinth or stand made for one sculpture (provisional until a page attests it).
notes: Stands, plinths and pedestals sold for displaying sculpture on 1stDibs.

name: back saw
definition: push-stroke hand saw whose thin blade is stiffened by a brass or steel back, for joinery cuts (tenon, dovetail, gents patterns).
notes: Axminster sells Back Saws as a category; the stiffened push-stroke form is neither panel saw nor backed pull saw (dozuki

name: coping saw
definition: hand saw with a thin, fine blade tensioned in a deep U-shaped frame, turned in the frame to cut curves in wood.
notes: Sold under its own name (Lee Valley saw types); frame form differs from hacksaw and scroll saw.

name: vertical panel saw
definition: wall-standing frame machine whose circular saw runs on a vertical guide to cut full sheets held upright.
notes: Axminster lists Panel Saws as a machine class; construction class changes the body (memo 4b.3).

name: reciprocating saw
definition: hand-held power saw with a long blade driven back and forth in line with the body, for demolition and rough cuts.
notes: Own Toolstation saw group; form differs from jigsaw (in-line blade, no shoe-guided curve cutting).

name: plunge saw [track saw]
definition: circular saw whose blade plunges down from a sprung housing and that runs on a guide rail for straight sheet cuts.
notes: Sold and compared apart from circular saws; plunge housing and rail fitting change the form (C10).

name: cut-off saw [disc cutter]
definition: hand-held engine or electric saw with a large abrasive or diamond disc behind a guard, for concrete, stone and steel.
notes: Own saw group at Toolstation; large guarded disc form, neither circular saw nor angle grinder.

name: contractor table saw
definition: table saw on an open stand with the motor hung behind the table, between jobsite and hybrid types.
notes: Rockler lists contractor saws as a class beside jobsite and cabinet; construction class is a kind (memo 4b.3).

name: straight-line rip saw
definition: industrial machine whose chain-driven bed feeds boards past a fixed blade to rip a straight edge.
notes: Grizzly lists Rip saws as a table-saw class (memo S16); feed bed changes the body.

name: single-edged pull saw [kataba]
definition: Japanese pull saw with teeth on one edge only and no back, for deeper crosscuts and rips than a dozuki allows.
notes: Woodcraft and Lee Valley sell kataba as a type; no tree kind covers it. Provisional like its siblings (C11, CV-27).

name: keyhole saw [pad saw, drywall saw]
definition: narrow pointed hand saw blade on a handle, for starting cuts from a drilled hole or cutting plasterboard.
notes: Lee Valley lists keyhole saws as a saw type; narrow unsupported blade differs from panel saw.

name: bow saw [buck saw]
definition: saw with a coarse blade tensioned in a bow or H frame, for crosscutting logs and timber.
notes: Lee Valley lists buck saws; a bow saw for logs is C1 (K-173 wood-cutting); pruning saws stay C2.

name: kindling splitter
definition: cast-iron frame with a fixed upward blade, into which a small log is struck with a hammer to split kindling.
notes: Sold as its own item (Roughneck); fixed-blade frame form is neither wedge, maul nor powered log splitter.

name: detail sander
definition: hand-held sander with a small triangular (delta) pad that vibrates, for corners and narrow areas.
notes: Own Toolstation sander group; pad shape and motion differ from random-orbit and belt sanders.

name: sheet sander [orbital finishing sander]
definition: hand-held sander with a rectangular pad moving in small orbits, taking a cut-down abrasive sheet.
notes: Sold apart from random-orbit sanders; rectangular orbital pad is a different form.

name: drywall sander
definition: sander with a large round head on a long pole and dust extraction, for plasterboard walls and ceilings.
notes: Long-reach pole form, sold under its own name by tool retailers.

name: oscillating spindle sander [bobbin sander]
definition: bench machine with an abrasive sleeve on a spindle that rotates and moves up and down through a table, for curves.
notes: Workshop machine sold under its own name; spindle form differs from belt and disc sanders.

name: belt and disc sander
definition: bench machine combining a sanding belt and a sanding disc on one motor.
notes: Combination machine listed as a class by a fetched seller (C-10), like the planer-thicknesser.

name: wall chaser
definition: hand-held machine with twin diamond discs that cuts parallel channels in masonry for cables and pipes.
notes: Toolstation sells it in the grinder family; twin-disc guarded form differs from the angle grinder.

name: biscuit jointer
definition: hand-held power tool that plunges a small circular blade sideways to cut slots for joining biscuits.
notes: Sold under its own name; plunge-cutter form; filed with routers as a slot-cutting power tool.

name: router table
definition: table with a router mounted beneath its top and a fence, holding the work to be passed over the bit.
notes: Toolstation workshop tools lists router tables; a work-holding table like the workbench (C1.6, K-190), not a part.

name: magnetic drill
definition: portable drill press on an electromagnetic base that clamps to steel, usually with annular cutters.
notes: Made only for the magnetic mount and its body differs (C12(a)); sold apart from pillar drills.

name: hand drill [wheel brace]
definition: hand-cranked geared drill with a side wheel and a chuck, for small holes.
notes: Tooled-Up lists Stanley 105 hand drill beside braces; geared form differs from the sweep brace.

name: pipe wrench
definition: heavy adjustable wrench with a hook jaw and serrated teeth that bite round pipe.
notes: Own Toolstation spanner type; jaw form differs from the adjustable wrench.

name: basin wrench
definition: long-shafted wrench with a pivoting jaw for tap and fitting nuts behind basins.
notes: Plumbing type sold under its own name; jaw-on-shaft form.

name: box spanner
definition: tubular spanner with hexagon ends, turned by a bar through a hole.
notes: Own spanner type; tube form differs from ring and socket wrenches.

name: block plane
definition: small one-hand plane with a low-angle bevel-up blade, for end grain and chamfers.
notes: Woodcraft sells block planes as a type; compared by role like smoother and jack (memo 4b.1).

name: shoulder plane
definition: narrow plane whose blade spans the full width of the sole, for trimming rebates and tenon shoulders.
notes: Own plane type at Woodcraft; open-sided form differs from bench planes.

name: router plane
definition: plane with a cutter hung below a flat base, for levelling grooves and recesses to depth.
notes: Own plane type at Woodcraft; base-and-hanging-cutter form.

name: plough plane
definition: plane with a fence and depth stop and interchangeable narrow cutters, for grooves along the grain.
notes: Named by the harvester on the Woodcraft page; fenced grooving form. Page does not show it in the logged gave text (†).

name: rasp
definition: steel bar or blade with individually raised teeth, for fast shaping of wood and soft materials.
notes: Axminster sells Files & Rasps apart; the leaf names rasps but holds no kind; tooth form differs from cut files.

name: combination lathe-mill
definition: metal lathe with a milling head on a column over the bed, one machine for turning and milling.
notes: Grizzly lists combo lathe/mills as a class: combination machine kind (C-10).

name: club hammer [lump hammer]
definition: short-handled heavy double-faced hammer for driving chisels and light demolition.
notes: Own Toolstation hammer type; heavy double-faced head differs from claw hammer and sledgehammer.

name: brick hammer
definition: hammer with a square striking face and a chisel blade, for cutting and setting bricks.
notes: Own hammer type; face-and-blade head differs from claw and pein hammers.

name: ball-pein hammer
definition: engineer's hammer with a flat face and a rounded pein, for metalwork and riveting.
notes: Own hammer type sold apart; head form differs.

name: cross-pein hammer [Warrington]
definition: hammer with a flat face and a wedge-shaped pein across the handle, for starting pins and tacks.
notes: Own hammer type; head form differs.

name: slater's hammer
definition: roofer's hammer with a pointed pick, a side nail claw and a blade for cutting and holing slates.
notes: Own hammer type; no generic kind covers its pick-and-blade head.

name: sledgehammer
definition: long-handled heavy hammer swung with both hands, for demolition and driving stakes.
notes: Own hammer type; two-handed long-handled form differs from the club hammer.

name: punch
definition: hardened steel rod struck with a hammer to mark centres, drive pins or set nails.
notes: Highland and Axminster sell punches with hammers; a struck tool family no kind covers.

name: nail puller [cat's paw]
definition: short bar with a claw tip driven under a nail head to lever it out.
notes: Sold under its own name; short claw-tip bar differs from the wrecking bar.

name: pry bar [flat bar]
definition: thin flat steel bar with bevelled ends and nail slots, for prising trim and boards.
notes: Tooled-Up sells pry bars apart from wrecking bars; thin flat form differs.

name: lifting bar [pinch bar]
definition: long heavy straight bar with a chisel or point end, used as a lever to lift slabs and heavy items.
notes: Own bar type at Tooled-Up; straight lever form, no claw.

name: plasma cutter
definition: machine that cuts metal with an electric arc through a constricted gas jet, sold and compared with welders.
notes: Toolstation and Bigweld sell it in welding; no cutting leaf fits a thermal cutter, so filed with welding machines (†).

name: gas soldering torch
definition: hand-held butane or propane torch for soldering, brazing and heating in trade and repair work.
notes: General soldering equipment is C1 (jewellery torches C4, K-171); a flame tool unlike the iron.

name: saw stand
definition: folding or wheeled stand that holds a mitre or table saw at working height, often with outrigger supports.
notes: Sold with workbenches and trestles (Toolstation); a work support like the sawhorse (C1.6).

name: line laser level
definition: self-levelling laser projecting horizontal and vertical lines for setting out.
notes: Toolstation lists laser levels beside spirit levels; instrument type is the kind (memo 4b.4).

name: rotary laser level
definition: laser with a spinning head that sweeps a 360-degree level plane, read by a detector on site.
notes: Sold apart from line lasers; rotating form and site range differ.

name: optical level [dumpy level]
definition: telescope on a tripod that sights a level line onto a staff, for site levels.
notes: Own instrument type at Toolstation.

name: angle finder
definition: dial, bevel or digital gauge that measures and transfers angles.
notes: Own Toolstation instrument; measures angles, which square and marking gauge do not.

name: detector [stud, pipe and cable detector]
definition: handheld device that senses studs, metal pipes or live cables behind a surface.
notes: Own Toolstation group; instrument type.

name: moisture meter
definition: instrument that measures moisture in timber or building materials.
notes: Instrument type sold apart; trade measuring tool is C1 (K-147).

name: infrared thermometer
definition: handheld non-contact thermometer that reads surface temperature from infrared radiation.
notes: Sold as a trade inspection tool (K-147); instrument type.

name: inspection camera [endoscope]
definition: camera on a flexible probe with a screen, for looking inside walls, pipes and machines.
notes: Sold under its own name in detection tools; instrument type.

name: sound level meter
definition: instrument that measures sound pressure level in decibels.
notes: Instrument type on the Toolstation page; site and trade measuring (K-147).

name: clamp meter
definition: electrical meter whose jaws close round a conductor to measure current without breaking the circuit.
notes: Fluke sells clamp meters apart from multimeters; jaw form differs.

name: oscilloscope
definition: instrument that displays electrical signals as waveforms, handheld or bench (ScopeMeter is a Fluke name).
notes: Electronics-work instrument is C1 (K-147); ScopeMeter is a trade name, so the kind is generic (†).

name: single ladder [leaning ladder]
definition: one-section ladder leaned against a support.
notes: No sliding sections, so not an extension ladder; ladder form is the kind (memo 4b.5).

name: roof ladder
definition: ladder with wheels and a ridge hook, laid on a pitched roof.

name: tripod ladder [garden ladder]
definition: ladder with a single rear leg forming a tripod, for uneven ground and hedges.
notes: Ladders are C1 whatever the use; tripod form differs (reading of 'garden ladder' †).

name: engine stand
definition: wheeled stand that holds an engine by its block and lets it rotate for rebuild work.
notes: Toolstation jacks & stands group; vehicle-service tool is C1 (K-13); form unlike axle stand.

name: transmission jack
definition: jack with a saddle that lifts and holds a gearbox for removal and fitting.
notes: Own type on the jacks page; vehicle-service tool (K-13).

name: scissor jack
definition: jack lifted by a screw closing a diamond of linked arms.
notes: Scissor mechanism differs from trolley and bottle jacks; harvester's 'scissor stand' read as scissor jack (†).

name: backhoe loader
definition: wheeled machine with a front loader bucket and a rear digging arm.
notes: Self-propelled digging machine is C1 (K-194); two-ended form differs from excavator and loader.

name: pallet truck [pallet jack]
definition: hand-pulled or powered low truck whose forks slide under a pallet and lift it just clear of the floor.
notes: Low-lift pallet mover differs from forklift (no mast) and from dollies; drive is an attribute.

name: tool chest
definition: drawered or lidded top box for tools, set on a bench or roller cabinet.
notes: Tooled-Up sells tool chests apart from roller cabinets; no casters, so its own container form.

name: site chest [jobsite box]
definition: large lockable steel box for storing tools on site or in a van.
notes: Own storage type; container form and security role differ from toolbox and chest.

name: tool pouch
definition: belt-worn pouch or holder carrying tools and fixings at hand.
notes: Worn container for one task's tools is C1 (K-132); differs from the tool bag.

name: surface pressure pump
definition: surface-mounted general-purpose pump that draws water and delivers it under pressure.
notes: General-purpose pumps are C1 (K-175); surface form differs from submersible and transfer pumps.

name: tungsten electrode
definition: non-consumable tungsten rod held in a TIG torch to carry the arc.

name: brazing rod
definition: filler alloy rod or wire for brazing joints.
notes: Filler consumable like welding rod and solder (K-12).

name: soldering and brazing flux
definition: paste, liquid or powder that cleans joint surfaces for soldering or brazing.
notes: Consumable of soldering and brazing, filed beside solder by K-12 (†: K-12 names solder, not flux).

name: Lintel
definition: beam of steel, concrete or timber set over a door or window opening to carry the wall above.
notes: Own shop group beside bricks and blocks; structural element no tree kind covers; material is an attribute.

name: Roof tile
definition: clay, concrete or slate unit laid in overlapping courses as a roof covering (slates included).
notes: Sold under its own name; unit covering, not a sheet, so roofing sheet does not cover it; material an attribute.

name: Roof shingle
definition: strip of bitumen felt or wood laid in overlapping courses as a roof covering (shed and garden-building roofs).

name: Roofing felt or membrane
definition: roll of bitumen felt or synthetic membrane laid as a roof covering or underlay.

name: Garage door

name: Door frame (door lining)
definition: frame or lining set sold to hang a door in an opening.
notes: Sold apart from the door leaf; a different object from the door, which covers leaves and complete sets.

name: Roof window
definition: window made to be fitted in the slope or flat of a roof (flat-roof windows included).
notes: Body and flashing made only for a roof mount (C12 a); shops shelve roof windows apart from wall windows.

name: Coach screw
definition: heavy hexagon-head wood screw driven with a spanner for structural timber fixings.
notes: Own Toolstation group; heavy structural screw distinct from the wood screw by form and drive.

name: Door knocker
definition: hinged knocker and plate fixed to an outside door.
notes: Front-door furniture shelved beside letter plates (Screwfix); no lock or security role, so not B8.

name: Conduit
definition: rigid or flexible tube through which mains cables are run.
notes: Cable-management product sold under its own name; not a cable or clip.

name: Trunking
definition: surface channel with a clip-on lid that carries and hides cables.
notes: Own cable-management type; form differs from conduit (open channel with lid).

name: Junction box
definition: enclosure in which mains cables are joined.
notes: Wiring accessory sold under its own name; not a switch, socket or rose.

name: Cable tie
definition: plastic or metal strap with a ratchet that bundles or fixes cables.
notes: Sold under its own name in cable management; general use, so no host category under S3.

name: Circuit breaker
definition: automatic switch for a consumer unit that breaks a circuit on overload or earth leakage (MCB, RCD, RCBO).

name: Plug adaptor
definition: plug-in unit that gives one socket-outlet two or more outlets or a different socket type.
notes: Own Screwfix group beside plugs and leads; no flex, so not an extension lead.

name: Flexible hose (tap connector)
definition: braided flexible hose with fittings that connects a tap, cistern or appliance to the supply pipe.

name: Water hammer arrester
definition: device fitted in a supply pipe that absorbs pressure shocks (water hammer).
notes: Sold under its own name; not a valve or tap. Weakest of the plumbing additions.

name: Soil and drain pipe
definition: large-bore pipe and fittings that carry waste from toilets and drains to the sewer, above or below ground.

name: Drainage channel
definition: surface channel with a grating that collects water from a drive, patio or floor.

name: Shower wall panel

name: jetty or pontoon

name: shop

name: hotel

name: office building

notes: Offices category for sale (10 listings).

name: warehouse

name: industrial unit

name: boathouse
definition: a building for keeping boats, on or beside water.
notes: Boathouse structure on a marina sold with moorage assumable; the structure is the item.

name: cart shed

name: granary
definition: a building for storing grain that a person can stand in.
notes: Granary listed as a farm building type in a national catalogue; entry on page contents.

name: dovecote
definition: a building for housing doves or pigeons that a person can enter.
notes: Dove cotes listed as a farm building type in a national catalogue.

name: decking
definition: a raised timber or composite platform built in place, including one built for a tent, yurt or tipi.
notes: Decking kits sold to build a deck, with optional handrails.

name: patio
definition: a laid paved or hard surface outside a building.
notes: Patio costed as a laid project including groundwork and installer.

name: Balance beam
definition: raised narrow beam on supports made for gymnastics balance training and competition.
notes: Gopher sells beams as their own apparatus type; empty Gymnastics leaf gets its kinds.

name: Parallel bars
definition: pair of equal-height rails on uprights made for men's gymnastics and training.

name: Uneven bars
definition: pair of rails set at different heights made for women's gymnastics.
notes: Sold as a distinct bar apparatus; body differs from parallel bars.

name: Horizontal bar
definition: single high or training bar on uprights for swings and release moves; a kids' single training bar is a named form.

name: Pommel horse
definition: padded body on legs with two handles (pommels) made for gymnastics circles and swings.
notes: AAI pommel horse sold as its own apparatus.

name: Vault board (springboard)
definition: sprung take-off board used for vaulting and gymnastics jumps.
notes: Vault boards sold as their own apparatus category.

name: HEMA chest protector (plastron)

name: HEMA gorget

name: HEMA fencing trousers

name: Lamé

name: Fencing glove
definition: padded glove with a cuff worn on the weapon hand in fencing.

name: Underarm protector (fencing plastron)
definition: half-jacket worn under the fencing jacket on the weapon-arm side, rated to FIE 800 N where certified.

name: Fencing chest protector
definition: rigid plastic chest guard worn under the fencing jacket.
notes: Sold separately from the underarm protector on the fetched page.

name: Fencing breeches

name: Fencing shoe

name: Jazz shoe

name: Character shoe
definition: heeled dance shoe with a strap, made for stage and character dance.
notes: Dance shoe type sold under its own name on the dancewear shop.

name: Air bike (fan bike)

name: Recumbent cross trainer (recumbent stepper)

name: Camping hammock
definition: suspended fabric bed hung between trees for sleeping outdoors; a garden hammock is not E2.
notes: Shelter-and-sleep type sold under its own name beside tarps.

name: Sleeping-bag liner
definition: thin bag of silk, cotton or fleece used inside a sleeping bag for warmth or hygiene.
notes: Sold as its own shelf by outdoor shops; not a part (used alone too).

name: Bothy bag (group shelter)
definition: windproof fabric bag that several people sit inside as an emergency shelter.
notes: Harvested shelters on the bivvy page are group shelters, a different body.

name: Table-tennis ball
definition: 40 mm celluloid-free plastic ball made for table tennis; star rating is an attribute.
notes: Ball kinds exist for every racket sport; Revspin sells balls.

name: Table-tennis robot
definition: ball-throwing machine that feeds table-tennis balls for practice.
notes: Training machine sold under its own name on the TT shop.

name: Badminton string
definition: string sold to string a badminton racket, by the set or the reel.
notes: Parts axis is the object served; new leaf Badminton rackets, as tennis string.

name: Badminton net
definition: net and posts or net alone sold for badminton.
notes: Net sold for the one sport (E2-2 net rule).

name: Complete golf set
definition: packaged set of clubs, usually with a bag, sold as one product.
notes: Package sets are a shelf of their own and compared as sets.

name: Utility iron (driving iron)
definition: long iron with a hollow or wide-soled iron head made to replace a long iron or hybrid.
notes: Club type is the choice level; iron head differs from the hybrid wood-like head.

name: Archery shooting glove
definition: three-finger glove worn on the drawing hand to draw and release the string.

name: Bow sling
definition: wrist or finger strap that keeps a bow in the archer's hand at release.
notes: Worn by the archer (K-163 class of arm guard and tab), sold on the same shelf.

name: Ski pole
definition: pole with a grip, strap and basket used in alpine and touring skiing.
notes: Used across alpine and touring: general leaf (C14 b).

name: Climbing skin
definition: strip of mohair or nylon plush fixed to a ski or splitboard base for climbing.
notes: Accessory made for one object (touring ski): parts leaf.

name: Snowboard binding
definition: non-release binding with highback and straps that fixes a boot to a snowboard.

name: Snowboard boot
definition: soft or stiff boot made to fit a snowboard binding.
notes: Boot made for one sport, like ski boot (P1).

name: Cross-country ski boot
definition: light boot with a Nordic binding interface made for cross-country skiing.
notes: Boot made for one sport; interface is a C13 platform.

name: Splitboard
definition: snowboard that splits into two ski-like halves for climbing and rejoins for descent.
notes: Like the touring ski (E-16): own body and shelf.

name: Swim fins
definition: rubber or silicone fins worn on the feet for swimming, snorkelling or diving.
notes: Used across swimming and diving: general water leaf (C14 b).

name: Snorkel
definition: breathing tube with mouthpiece for swimming face-down at the surface.
notes: Defined by snorkelling use; front-mounted swim snorkels are named forms.

name: Swim cap
definition: silicone, latex or fabric cap worn for swimming.
notes: Swim gear at the general leaf, like swim goggles.

name: Pull buoy
definition: foam float held between the legs for arm-only swim training.
notes: Swim training aid sold under its own name.

name: Kickboard
definition: foam board held in front for kick-only swim training.
notes: Swim training aid sold under its own name.

name: Kite control bar
definition: bar with lines and safety release used to steer one kite.
notes: Accessory made for one object (kite); new parts leaf Kites.

name: Kite harness
definition: waist or seat harness that hooks the rider to the kite bar.
notes: Worn gear is never a part; made for kite and wind sports.

name: Kiteboard
definition: twin-tip or directional board ridden while pulled by a kite.
notes: Board kind like surfboard; shops sell it apart.

name: SUP paddle
definition: single-blade paddle made for stand-up paddleboarding.
notes: P7 paddle follows its board; parts leaf Stand-up paddleboards.

name: Foilboard
definition: short buoyant board made to carry a hydrofoil for wing, kite or surf foiling.
notes: Board body differs from surfboard and kiteboard; shop category.

name: Hydrofoil
definition: mast, fuselage and wings fitted under a foilboard.
notes: Part made for one object (foilboard); new parts leaf Foilboards.

name: Surf leash
definition: cord that ties a surfboard to the rider's ankle.
notes: Accessory made for one object (surfboard): parts leaf Surfboards.

name: Surf fin
definition: fin fitted to a surfboard's fin box.
notes: Part made for surfboards.

name: Surf wax
definition: wax rubbed on a surfboard deck for grip.
notes: Used up on one object (S3).

name: Batting helmet
definition: helmet made for batting in baseball or softball.

name: Catcher's gear
definition: catcher's helmet or mask, chest protector and leg guards, as a set or piece.

name: Batting pads (cricket)
definition: leg guards worn by a cricket batter.
notes: Protective gear made for one sport, sold on the fetched page.

name: Cricket helmet

name: Cricket batting gloves

name: Wicket-keeping gloves

name: Stumps (wicket set)
definition: set of stumps and bails, fixed or on a base, made for cricket.

name: Goalkeeper gloves

name: Football goal
definition: goal frame with net made for football.
notes: Sold for the one sport.

name: Ice tool
definition: technical axe with a curved shaft and steep pick made for ice and mixed climbing.
notes: Body differs from walking ice axe (E2.16.4.02); MEC sells them apart.

name: Ice screw

name: Traction device (microspikes)

name: Kicking tee
definition: stand that holds a rugby ball upright for place kicks.

name: Padel racket cover

name: Pickleball shoe

name: Jon boat

name: Jet boat
definition: powerboat driven by a water jet.
notes: Aceboater jet boats with enclosed jet propulsion.

name: Tender
definition: small boat made to carry people and goods between a larger vessel and the shore.

name: eFoil
definition: electric powered hydrofoil board ridden standing (K-90).

definition: fixed-wing airplane with one piston engine.

name: Turboprop airplane
definition: fixed-wing airplane driven by one or more turboprop engines.
notes: Controller category Turboprop Aircraft.

name: Multi-engine piston airplane
definition: fixed-wing airplane with two or more piston engines.

name: Jet
definition: fixed-wing airplane driven by jet engines, from light and business jets to airliners.

name: Amphibian or floatplane
definition: fixed-wing airplane made to take off from and land on water.

name: Gyroplane

name: Hot-air balloon
definition: lighter-than-air aircraft lifted by heated air in an envelope.

name: Gas balloon
definition: lighter-than-air aircraft lifted by a light gas, without propulsion.
notes: Cameron GB1000 hydrogen gas balloon page.

name: Airship
definition: powered, steerable lighter-than-air aircraft.
notes: Zeppelin NT described as airship type with N07-100 and N07-101 variants.

name: Powered parachute
definition: aircraft with a parachute wing and a motorised cart below it.

name: Weight-shift trike
definition: powered hang-glider-type wing over a trike, steered by shifting weight.

name: Panoramic film camera
definition: film camera whose lens swings or whose body rotates to expose a wide panoramic frame (swing-lens and rotating cameras).

name: Extension tube
definition: lensless spacer ring or tube fitted between body and lens so the lens focuses closer; bellows units are a named form.

name: LED tube light
definition: handheld or mountable LED tube or bar giving constant light along its length (light wand).

name: Flag or net
definition: framed panel of opaque fabric or open net placed in front of a light to block or cut it (flags, cutters, single and double nets).

name: Overhead frame (butterfly)
definition: large frame, with stand mounts, that stretches a silk, solid or net over or beside a scene.
notes: B&H lists butterflies as a group; frame size and stand rigging differ from a portable reflector disc.

name: Speed ring
definition: ring that holds the rods of a softbox and fixes it to a light's modifier mount.
notes: B&H lists speed rings as their own group; sold apart from softboxes; the mount itself stays a C13 row.

name: Body-worn camera support
definition: vest with a spring arm or overhead strut that takes a camera's weight onto the operator's body (Easyrig, Steadicam).

name: Print washer
definition: tank or archival washer that removes fixer from prints with running water.
notes: B&H lists print washers as a group; no print-processing kind covers washing.

name: Negative carrier
definition: frame that holds a negative flat in an enlarger, made per enlarger and format.
notes: Freestyle sells negative carriers on their own; not an enlarger, easel or lens.

name: Contact printing frame (proof printer)
definition: glass-topped frame that holds negatives against paper for contact sheets.
notes: CRK lists the Paterson proof printer; exposure-stage tool no kind covers.

name: Fossil coral
definition: fossil coral, solitary or colonial, rough, polished or on matrix (a dead modern coral skeleton is F6.6.4.01).
notes: FossilEra category of its own; invertebrate group with no kind; organism group is the fossil choice level (memo 4b).

name: Fossil bivalve
definition: fossil clam, oyster, scallop or other bivalve shell, whole, opalised or on matrix.
notes: FossilEra category; organism group sellers open; no invertebrate kind covers bivalves.

name: Fossil brachiopod
definition: fossil lamp shell (brachiopod), loose, pyritised or on matrix.
notes: FossilEra category; brachiopods are neither molluscs nor echinoderms, so no kind covers them.

name: Bryozoan fossil
definition: fossil bryozoan colony (moss animal), such as Archimedes screw or fenestrate lace, on or off matrix.
notes: FossilEra category of its own; no invertebrate kind covers bryozoans.

name: Fossil crustacean
definition: fossil crab, lobster, shrimp or other crustacean, usually in a nodule or on matrix.
notes: FossilEra 'Crabs and lobsters' category (memo S1); one arthropod group sold together.

name: Fossil insect
definition: fossil insect or other terrestrial arthropod preserved in rock (an insect in amber or copal stays F6.3.5).
notes: FossilEra 'Insects' category; rock-preserved insects have no kind; amber inclusions remain an amber tag.

name: Fossil gastropod
definition: fossil snail shell (gastropod), whole, agatised or on matrix.
notes: FossilEra category; organism group with no kind; modern snail shells stay F6.6.1.

name: Graptolite
definition: fossil graptolite colony, usually on a shale slab.
notes: FossilEra category of its own; no invertebrate kind covers graptolites.

name: Fossil nautiloid
definition: fossil coiled nautiloid shell, whole, split or polished (straight nautiloids such as Orthoceras stay F6.3.1.03).
notes: FossilEra and UK Fossils (memo S29) sell nautilus apart from ammonites and belemnites.

name: Fossil sponge
definition: fossil sponge, whole or sectioned, loose or on matrix.
notes: FossilEra category; no invertebrate kind covers sponges.

name: Trace fossil
definition: fossil track, footprint, burrow, boring or coprolite left by an organism rather than its body.
notes: FossilEra trace-fossil category; leaf F6.3.4 Trace and microbial held only stromatolite.

name: Fossil mammal
definition: fossil tooth, bone or other part of a mammal, such as mammoth, cave bear or whale (`part` attribute).
notes: FossilEra category; vertebrate group with no kind beside dinosaur, fish and shark tooth.

name: Plant fossil
definition: fossil leaf, fern, frond, seed or cone, as an impression, compression or nodule (petrified wood is F6.3.3.01).
notes: FossilEra 'plant fossil' category apart from petrified wood; memo object 'fossil leaf' had no kind.

name: Fossil reptile, amphibian or synapsid
definition: fossil tooth, bone or skeleton of a non-dinosaur reptile (mosasaur, crocodile, plesiosaur), amphibian or synapsid.
notes: FossilEra groups these in one category; no vertebrate kind covers them (dinosaur kind excludes them).

name: Azurite
definition: copper carbonate hydroxide mineral specimen (blue crystals, nodules, with or without malachite).
notes: FossilEra species category; Strunz carbonates; mineral kinds are species sellers open (memo 4b).

name: Aragonite
definition: calcium carbonate (orthorhombic) mineral specimen (sputniks, clusters, flos-ferri).
notes: FossilEra species category; Strunz carbonates; distinct species from calcite.

name: Halite
definition: sodium chloride mineral specimen (cubic crystals, coloured or clear).
notes: FossilEra species category; Strunz halides beside fluorite.

name: Hematite
definition: iron oxide mineral specimen (specular, botryoidal or rose crystals, tumbled pieces).
notes: FossilEra species category; Strunz oxides.

name: Beryl
definition: uncut beryl specimen (aquamarine, morganite, heliodor, emerald crystals on or off matrix); cut stones are F6.5.
notes: FossilEra species category; uncut counterpart of beryl gems under the F-4 cut-state test.

name: Topaz (specimen)
definition: uncut topaz crystal or specimen on or off matrix; a faceted stone or cutting rough is F6.5.2.08, sharing its species_id.
notes: FossilEra species category; memo edge 5 names topaz in both F6.1 and F6.5; F6.1 half missing.

name: Turquoise
definition: copper aluminium phosphate mineral specimen (nuggets, veins on matrix, rough or polished, stabilised or not).
notes: FossilEra species category; first kind in Strunz phosphates; memo edge 2 files it as species.

name: Lapis lazuli
definition: uncut or polished lapis lazuli (lazurite-rich rock) specimen, with a Rocks alias; a cabochon is F6.5.
notes: Memo edge 2: seller treats it as a species, so F6.1 with a rock alias; FossilEra category.

name: Serpentine
definition: serpentine-group mineral or serpentinite specimen, rough, tumbled or polished, with a rock alias serpentinite.
notes: Sold on FossilEra's minerals page as its own category; edge 2 rule files it with minerals.

name: Feldspar
definition: uncut feldspar-group specimen (microcline, amazonite, labradorite, orthoclase, moonstone and sunstone rough or polished); cut stones are F6.5.
notes: Mineral group sold as its own category, like garnet (F6.1.9.02); named varieties become named forms.

name: Rhyolite
definition: fine-grained silica-rich extrusive igneous rock sample (including rainforest and wonderstone rhyolite).
notes: Rock type sold under its own name; igneous class; memo expects 50-70 rock kinds.

name: Porphyry
definition: igneous rock sample with large crystals in a fine-grained groundmass (e.g. Chinese writing stone).
notes: Rock type sold under its own name; igneous class; no kind covers it.

name: Fulgurite
definition: natural tube or crust of silica glass fused by lightning in sand or rock.
notes: Sold as its own category; not impact glass (F6.4.07); silica glass placed with quartz family, placement provisional.

name: HED meteorite
definition: achondrite of the howardite, eucrite and diogenite group, from asteroid Vesta.
notes: FossilEra and N's Mineral (memo S3, S7) both give HED its own category (C11 two regions).

name: Mesosiderite
definition: stony-iron meteorite of silicate breccia and iron-nickel metal in roughly equal parts.
notes: FossilEra 'Mesosiderites' category; stony-iron class beside pallasite; no kind covers it.

name: Achondrite
definition: stony meteorite without chondrules not covered by the lunar, Martian or HED kinds (aubrites, angrites, ureilites, primitive achondrites).
notes: FossilEra 'Achondrites' category; without it an aubrite or ureilite has no home; the chondrite split (section 14) stays.

name: Starfish (dried)
definition: dried whole starfish (sea star) kept as a specimen (a fossil starfish is F6.3.1.04; craft assortments C4).
notes: Sold by name in specimen lots; echinoderm leaf has coral and urchin test only.

name: Murex shell
definition: shell of a murex or rock snail (Muricidae).
notes: Popular family on Conchology and Catawiki lots; shell kind is the family (memo 4b).

name: Volute shell
definition: shell of a volute (Volutidae).
notes: Popular family at Conchology; shell kind is the family or popular group (memo 4b).

name: Brachiopod shell
definition: shell of a living-species brachiopod (lamp shell) kept as a specimen; fossil brachiopods are F6.3.1.08.
notes: Conchology popular group; brachiopods are not molluscs, so a new leaf value on the animal axis is needed.

name: Articulated skeleton
definition: real animal skeleton cleaned and articulated on a stand or in a case; animal group is an attribute.
notes: Skulls Unlimited and Oddities sell skeletons as their own type; no kind covers a whole skeleton.

name: Claw or tooth specimen
definition: real modern animal claw, talon or tooth kept as a specimen (fossil teeth are F6.3).
notes: Skulls Unlimited 'Claws and Teeth' collection; no kind covers loose claws or teeth.

name: Taxidermy reptile mount
definition: reptile skin preserved and mounted as in life (full mount or head).
notes: Mounts are split by animal group (memo 4b); bird and mammal only; alligator heads sold as mounts.

name: Specimen frame case
definition: glazed floating frame or case made to hold and display one specimen; one holding several (Riker tray) is B1.
notes: Holder made for one specimen follows it (S3, K-9); dome, stand and box do not cover a frame.

name: Ritual hand drum
definition: Small two-headed hand drum, often hourglass-shaped with pellets on cords, rattled or struck in a rite (damaru a named form); one sold for music is E3.
notes: Sound-makers hold only a slit drum; a membrane hand drum differs in form. Made for a rite F4, else E3 (K-110).

name: Ritual hand cymbals
definition: Pair of small thick cymbals joined by a cord, struck together in a rite (tingsha a named form); ones sold for meditation are E3.
notes: No handle and struck together: not a hand bell or bowl bell. Made for a rite F4, meditation E3 (K-110).

name: Memorial register [kakocho]
definition: Book or folding album made to record the names and death dates of the dead, kept at a household altar (kakocho a named form).
notes: Marks the dead (F4.6 first, step 14 before F5); a book, not a tablet; Japanese shops sell it beside ihai.

name: Dowsing rod
definition: Rod, pair of L-rods or forked rod made to be held for dowsing or divination; one sold as a survey or pipe-finding tool goes with tools.
notes: Esoteric shop sells dowsing rods beside pendulum, as a radiesthesia tool; no F4.5.2 kind covers a held rod.

name: Paper-streamer wand [gohei]
definition: Wand of zigzag paper or metal-foil streamers set at a shrine or household altar as the sign of the kami's presence (gohei, kinpei named forms).
notes: Kamidana shop sells it with shimenawa as a shrine fitting; no altar, image or implement kind covers it.

name: Vibrating cushion
definition: Cushion or pad with a built-in vibrator that the user sits or lies on for external stimulation; a cushion that only positions the body is B2.
notes: Own Orion category; cushion body differs from hand-held vibrators; vibrates, no earlier sub-family takes it (motor rule)

name: Labia spreader
definition: Straps or a frame with clamps or hooks that hold the labia apart, made to restrain the genitals during sex play.
notes: Holds open rather than pinches, so not a clamp; genital restraint leaf; sold under its own generic name.

name: Short sword
definition: Straight double-edged one-handed sword with a blade clearly shorter than an arming sword, often without a cross guard; gladius and xiphos are named forms.

name: Falchion
definition: Broad single-edged one-handed European sword, straight or slightly curved, often widening towards the point; messer and grosse messer are named forms.

name: Sword cane

name: Single-shot shotgun

definition: Metal truncheon with a central rod and two curved side prongs, used in pairs.

name: Fighting sickle (kama)
definition: Short-hafted sickle blade made as a weapon, often used in pairs; a garden sickle is C2.

name: Suppressor

name: Arrowhead

name: Cartridge case

name: Scope mount

name: CO2 capsule
definition: Sealed carbon dioxide cartridge (8 g, 12 g, 88 g) that powers CO2 air guns and launchers.

name: Poleaxe

name: Performance powerboat

name: Bass boat
definition: low, flat-decked freshwater fishing boat with raised casting decks, livewells and a high-power outboard.
notes: Sold and listed as its own class; built for inland casting, unlike the offshore sport-fishing boat.

name: Ski and wakeboard boat (tow boat)
definition: inboard powerboat built to tow water-skiers or wakeboarders, with a tow pylon or tower and a tuned wake.
notes: Ski and wake boats are a listed class with their own makers (MasterCraft, Malibu); inboard tow form.

name: Deck boat
definition: open powerboat with a wide beam carried forward to a large open bow deck, seating many on a V or tri-hull.
notes: Listed apart from the bowrider and pontoon boat; wide-bow hull differs from both.

name: Recumbent tricycle
definition: three-wheeled pedal cycle ridden in a reclined seat with the pedals in front (tadpole or delta layout).
notes: Shops sell recumbent trikes apart from recumbent bikes and upright adult tricycles; 11 harvested trike models misfiled.

name: Lead holder (clutch pencil)
definition: Holder whose clutch grips a thick graphite lead (2 mm or more) that drops when the button is pressed; sharpened in a lead pointer.
notes: JetPens lists Lead Holders (90 items) as its own category under Drafting Pencils beside Lead Pointers.

name: Digital back
definition: digital capture unit with sensor that replaces the film back of a medium- or large-format camera.
notes: Digital Transitions category of digital backs: Phase One IQ4, IQ3, IQ2 series for medium-format systems.

name: Tungsten light
definition: constant light with a tungsten-halogen lamp in an open-face or focusing housing (redhead, blonde); a tungsten Fresnel stays D4.3.2.03.
notes: Tungsten fixtures sold apart: ARRI Arrilite 1000 open-face, Fresnels; Lowel Tota-light tungsten halogen source.

name: HMI light
definition: daylight constant light with a metal-halide arc lamp run from a separate ballast; an HMI Fresnel stays D4.3.2.03.
notes: HMI heads sold with separate electronic ballast, e.g. ARRI Arrisun 5 kit, Compact 575 HMI.

name: Camera dolly
definition: wheeled platform or track dolly that moves a camera smoothly during a shot.
notes: B&H Camera Dollies category: platform and track dollies (Proaim, Vinten, E-Image, CAME-TV).

name: Camera slider
definition: short rail with a carriage that slides a camera in a straight line.
notes: B&H Camera Sliders category: rail and carriage sliders, manual and motorized (YC Onion, Konova, Libec).

name: Camera crane or jib
definition: counterweighted arm on a stand or base that raises, lowers and swings a camera.
notes: B&H Cranes and Jibs category: jib arms with counterweights (Libec JB40, JonyJib, Proaim Comet).

name: Camera pedestal or studio column stand
definition: wheeled column stand that raises and lowers a camera in a studio.
notes: Adorama Camera Stands and Pedestals: studio pedestals (Vinten Vision Ped, Libec P1000, Miller, Cartoni Lifto).

name: Black-and-white reversal film
definition: black-and-white film processed by reversal to a positive slide or cine print.
notes: Foma Fomapan R100 listed as black and white reversal (transparency) film, R-100 reversal process.

name: Film dryer
definition: cabinet or heated unit that dries developed film hanging in strips.
notes: JOBO Mistral 3 heated drying cabinet dries hanging roll film, 8 rolls in 15-30 minutes.

name: Darkroom thermometer

name: Darkroom graduate
definition: measuring cylinder or jug for mixing photographic chemistry.
notes: Paterson plastic graduate 5 oz sold in Film & Darkroom, resistant to photographic chemicals.

name: Print tongs
definition: tongs for moving prints between trays without touching the chemistry.
notes: Paterson print tongs, three colour-coded pairs, one per tray: developer, stop, fixer.

name: Camera screen protector
definition: film or glass sheet cut to protect one camera's rear screen.
notes: SmallRig screen protector SR5803 cut for named cameras: Fujifilm X100V, X-T5, Ricoh GR IV.

name: Focusing screen
definition: interchangeable ground-glass screen fitted in a camera's viewfinder.
notes: B&H SLR Camera Focusing Screens category: Nikon Type E, Pentax ML-60, each for named bodies.

name: Camera dry cabinet
definition: humidity-controlled cabinet made to store cameras and lenses against fungus.
notes: Sirui HC series electronic humidity control cabinet stores photographic gear against moisture.

name: Electronic starting system
definition: electronic start unit that gives the start signal by sound and light in place of a blank pistol.
notes: Gill Halo electronic starter: ring with 12 LEDs and tone or bang via speaker, replaces blanks.

name: Elliptical cross trainer
definition: standing cardio machine with foot pedals on an elliptical path and moving arm handles.
notes: Retailer lists Horizon elliptical cross trainers Andes 7.1 and 7i; shop page thin.

name: Strong cider
definition: apple cider of higher strength than the traditional styles (BJCP C2).
notes: Ace High Imperial cider about 8% ABV sold as imperial-strength craft cider; Secret Seven 8.2%.

name: data centre
definition: a building made to house computer servers and their power and cooling plant.
notes: No function kind covers it (not storing goods, not producing goods, not offices); leaf allows 5-10 kinds (memo 4).

name: shepherd's hut
definition: a small timber or tin-clad hut on a wheeled chassis made to stand in a garden or field as a room; with its own sink, toilet and entrance it is a tiny house on wheels.
notes: Sold under its own name by many makers; no garden-room kind fits a wheeled hut; dwelling test (K-63) keeps one home.

name: bunker
definition: an underground or blast-hardened shelter structure, such as a former military or civil-defence bunker or a buried survival shelter.
notes: LandSale type; function is shelter, which no kind covers; a bunker converted to a dwelling is a detached house.

name: garden kitchen
definition: a garden building or roofed structure fitted as a kitchen with worktops for cooking, whatever its walls.
notes: Parallel to the garden bar (filed by fitted purpose, KLFIX1); outdoor kitchen cabinetry sold alone stays B1.

name: field shelter
definition: an open-fronted shelter for horses or livestock standing in a field, fixed or on skids, that a person can stand in.
notes: Sold as its own category beside stable blocks; no stalls (not a stable block), no open store (not a barn).

name: patio cover
definition: a roofed open-sided structure on posts made to fix to a house wall over a patio or deck (veranda, Terrassenueberdachung).
notes: Made only for the wall mount, solid roof (C12a): not a freestanding gazebo, not an open-topped pergola.

name: toilet safety frame
definition: free-standing or toilet-fixed frame with armrests round a toilet that helps a person sit down and rise.
notes: Drive and Binsons sell 'toilet safety frames' apart from raised seats and grab bars; frame form no kind covers.

name: bath lift
definition: powered seat that lowers a person into the bath and raises them out again.
notes: Drive sells 'bath lifts' as own category; powered lowering seat differs in form from a shower chair.

name: tub transfer bench
definition: bench that straddles the bath wall so a person sits outside the bath and slides across into it.
notes: Drive lists 'transfer benches' apart from bath benches and stools; made for transfer, not only sitting to wash.

name: bed rail
definition: rail or assist handle fitted to a bed to prevent falls or help a person sit up and stand.
notes: Invacare sells bed rails; fits any home bed, so not an H2.12 part; bed-care leaf.

name: penile traction device

definition: powered lift fitted inside a car or on its hitch that raises a mobility scooter or wheelchair into or onto the vehicle.

name: low-vision monocular

name: tubular bandage

name: liquid bandage
definition: spray or liquid that dries to a protective film over a small wound.

definition: shotgun shell loaded with one heavy projectile.
notes: Able Ammo has a 12 Gauge Slugs category.

name: Seven-inch single record
definition: Small 7-inch vinyl disc, usually 45 rpm, carrying one or two songs; sold apart from LPs and 12-inch singles.
notes: Shop menu lists 7" vinyl singles as its own category.

name: Twelve-inch single record
definition: Vinyl single on a 12-inch disc, usually 45 or 33 1/3 rpm, with one to a few tracks and often remixes (maxi-single), for DJ and club use; sold apart from LPs.
notes: Shop menu lists 12" singles as its own category.

name: Card toploader
definition: rigid plastic holder made to hold one card, sold apart from soft sleeves.
notes: The Pennysleever shop menu has Toploaders as its own category.

name: Card sleeve
definition: soft clear sleeve made to hold one card (penny sleeve), sold apart from rigid toploaders.
notes: The Pennysleever shop menu lists Card Sleeves as a category separate from Toploaders.

name: Stamp hinge
definition: small folded gummed paper piece that fixes one stamp to an album page, sold apart from mounts.
notes: Harry Edelman has a Stamp Hinges category beside separate Hawid, Prinz and Showgard mount headings.
